description.value: The study integrated fMRI food-cue reactivity with ecological momentary assessment to examine whether individual differences in BOLD response moderated the relationship between craving and binge eating in women with BN symptoms.

value: We hypothesize that women with BN will exhibit significant increases in BOLD response to palatable, high fat and high calorie food cues compared to neutral cues in the following a priori regions of the appetitive network: amygdala, posterior and anterior insula, OFC, and the striatum.

Finally, we hypothesize that greater increases in activation in a priori ROIs (appetitive network) will moderate the relationship between craving and binge eating in the naturalistic EMA data, such that individuals with increases in activation in response to food cues will exhibit greater increases in craving prior to binges.
